@graph.articleBody: Your past clients like you. Your Instagram followers like your posts. But when a stranger in your town types "real estate agent near me" into Google, does your name come up at all? Being liked and being found are two different jobs. This guide covers the second one: how an agent gets found in local search, with the quirks that are specific to your business. Many agents work from a home office or a desk at a brokerage, and that changes how you handle your address on Google. mainEntity.name: Should a real estate agent use a home address on Google Business Profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you do not serve customers at your home address, Google says to remove your address from your Business Profile. A service-area business should hide its business address from customers, so most agents who work from home keep their address private.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a virtual office or P.O. box as my address?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says that a rented mailing address where you do not operate, also known as a virtual office, is not eligible for a Business Profile, and that P.O. boxes or mailboxes at remote locations are not acceptable.

mainEntity.name: How many service areas can I list?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says you can set up to 20 service areas based on cities, postal codes or other areas you serve. List only the places where you really take clients.

mainEntity.name: Can I give clients a gift for leaving a review?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says offering free or discounted goods or services in exchange for reviews is strictly prohibited. Ask every client in the same way, with your profile's review link or QR code, and do not offer anything in return.

mainEntity.name: Can I pay to rank higher in local results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google states that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Relevance, distance and prominence decide local results, and reviews and links to your website feed prominence.
